openwrt_wiki.einleitung: OpenWrt One is based on the MediaTek Filogic 820 SoC and has WiFi 6, dual-band, 3x3/2x2, 1x 2.5Gbit WAN, 1x 1Gbit LAN, 1GB DDR4 RAM, 256 MiB NAND, 16 MiB NOR (for recovery), M.2 2242/2230 socket for NVMe SSD (PCIe gen 2 x1), USB-C Serial console, USB 2.0, and Power over Ethernet (PoE) with IEEE 802.3af/at compliance to provide power to the One via the RJ-45 2.5 Gbps WAN port.
openwrt_wiki.m2_hinweis: Note that recent (2025-10) batches of the OpenWrt One have an M.2 slot with a detached post at the 2230 position and the shipped product contains no way to attach the post.
openwrt_wiki.erster_start: NAND/NOR-Schalter auf NAND (oben = NAND, unten = NOR). 1G-Port = LAN (25.10). Strom: Option 1 USB Type-C an der Rueckseite, Option 2 PoE (PD) ueber den 2.5G-Port links neben USB-C; CAT6 fuer volle 2.5G. 2.5G = WAN. Beim Booten blinken die 3 Lichter vorn nacheinander, gruen dauerhaft = fertig. 192.168.1.1, root ohne Passwort. Ein Nutzer meldete vertauschtes LAN/WAN ab Werk (forum.openwrt.org/t/reversed-lan-wan-in-freshly-opened-openwrt-one).
openwrt_wiki.vorinstalliert: Each OpenWrt One comes flashed with the current release firmware based on the manufacturing batch date. LuCI web UI will be installed.
openwrt_wiki.wlan: mt76; AX, WPA2/WPA3, 20/40 MHz auf 2.4 GHz, 80/160 MHz auf 5 GHz, TWT
openwrt_wiki.offload: Hardware Flow Offloading, Wireless Ethernet Dispatch (WED) fuer 5 GHz
openwrt_wiki.upgrade_usb: FAT32-USB-Stick mit openwrt-mediatek-filogic-openwrt_one-squashfs-sysupgrade.itb, Strom weg, Stick in USB-A, NAND-Schalter, Reset-Knopf hinten (beschriftet Reset) halten, Strom an, loslassen wenn alle LEDs aus, warten bis mittlere LED gruen
openwrt_wiki.nand_recovery_initramfs: NAND-Schalter, Knopf an der Front halten beim Einschalten, loslassen wenn alle LEDs aus -> Recovery-initramfs
openwrt_wiki.nor_recovery: Schalter auf NOR, USB-Stick mit snand-preloader.bin + factory.ubi, Front-Knopf halten beim Einschalten -> NOR-Recovery flasht NAND komplett neu
openwrt_wiki.uart_recovery: mtk_uartboot ueber USB-C-Konsole (115200), dann Bootmenue: NOR entsperren (Jumper NOR WP), FIP/BL2/Recovery per TFTP (One 192.168.11.11, Server 192.168.11.23, 1G-LAN-Port) nach NOR schreiben
openwrt_wiki.konsole: Eingebauter USB-C-Seriell-Port an der Front (neben USB-A), integrierter USB-Seriell-Wandler, erscheint als ttyACM0 / 'OpenWrt One'; 115200 8N1, keine Flusskontrolle; Datenkabel noetig; Port nur fuer Konsole, nicht fuer Strom
openwrt_wiki.gehaeuse: Dimensions: 148 x 100.5 mm - compatible with Banana Pi BPI-R4 case design.
openwrt_wiki.notes: NOR is used for recovery. In normal operations the router should be booted from NAND. Offizielle Haendler bei SFC.

openwrt_image_mk.Device/openwrt_one:
DEVICE_VENDOR := OpenWrt
  DEVICE_MODEL := One
  DEVICE_DTS := mt7981b-openwrt-one
  DEVICE_DTS_DIR := ../dts
  DEVICE_DTC_FLAGS := --pad 4096
  DEVICE_DTS_LOADADDR := 0x43f00000
  DEVICE_PACKAGES := kmod-mt7915e kmod-mt7981-firmware mt7981-wo-firmware kmod-rtc-pcf8563 kmod-usb3 kmod-phy-airoha-en8811h
  KERNEL_LOADADDR := 0x44000000
  KERNEL := kernel-bin | libdeflate-gzip
  KERNEL_INITRAMFS := kernel-bin | lzma | \
	fit lzma $$(KDIR)/image-$$(firstword $$(DEVICE_DTS)).dtb with-initrd | pad-to 64k
  KERNEL_INITRAMFS_SUFFIX := .itb
  KERNEL_IN_UBI := 1
  UBOOTENV_IN_UBI := 1
  IMAGES := sysupgrade.itb
  IMAGE_SIZE := $$(shell expr 64 + $$(CONFIG_TARGET_ROOTFS_PARTSIZE))m
  IMAGE/sysupgrade.itb := append-kernel | fit gzip $$(KDIR)/image-$$(firstword $$(DEVICE_DTS)).dtb external-with-rootfs | pad-rootfs | append-metadata
  ARTIFACTS := \
	nor-preloader.bin nor-bl31-uboot.fip \
	snand-preloader.bin snand-bl31-uboot.fip \
	factory.ubi snand-factory.bin nor-factory.bin
  ARTIFACT/nor-preloader.bin		:= mt7981-bl2 nor-ddr4
  ARTIFACT/nor-bl31-uboot.fip		:= mt7981-bl31-uboot openwrt_one-nor
  ARTIFACT/snand-preloader.bin		:= mt7981-bl2 spim-nand-ubi-ddr4
  ARTIFACT/snand-bl31-uboot.fip		:= mt7981-bl31-uboot openwrt_one-snand
  ARTIFACT/factory.ubi			:= ubinize-image fit squashfs-sysupgrade.itb
  ARTIFACT/snand-factory.bin		:= mt7981-bl2 spim-nand-ubi-ddr4 | pad-to 256k | \
					   mt7981-bl2 spim-nand-ubi-ddr4 | pad-to 512k | \
					   mt7981-bl2 spim-nand-ubi-ddr4 | pad-to 768k | \
					   mt7981-bl2 spim-nand-ubi-ddr4 | pad-to 1024k | \
					   ubinize-image fit squashfs-sysupgrade.itb
  ARTIFACT/nor-factory.bin		:= mt7981-bl2 nor-ddr4 | pad-to 256k | \
					   append-openwrt-one-eeprom | pad-to 1024k | \
					   mt7981-bl31-uboot openwrt_one-nor | pad-to 512k | \
					   append-image-stage initramfs.itb
  UBINIZE_OPTS := -E 5
  BLOCKSIZE := 128k
  PAGESIZE := 2048
  UBINIZE_PARTS := fip=:$(STAGING_DIR_IMAGE)/mt7981_openwrt_one-snand-u-boot.fip \
		   $(if $(IB),recovery=:$(STAGING_DIR_IMAGE)/mediatek-filogic-openwrt_one-initramfs.itb,\
			      recovery=:$(KDIR)/tmp/$$(KERNEL_INITRAMFS_IMAGE)) \
		   $(if $(wildcard $(TOPDIR)/openwrt-mediatek-filogic-openwrt_one-calibration.itb), calibration=:$(TOPDIR)/openwrt-mediatek-filogic-openwrt_one-calibration.itb)

bpi_docs.Debugging: Console via USB-C port or 3-pin header, 10-pin JTAG/SWD header for main SoC
bpi_docs.Misc: Reset and User buttons; Boot select switch: NAND (regular) or NOR (recovery); 2x PWM LEDs, 2x Ethernet LED (GPIO driven); EM6324 External hardware watchdog; NXP PCF8563TS (I2C) RTC with battery backup holder for CR1220 coin-cell

sfc.Preis: From: $125 USD; 'Priced starting at US$125 for a complete OpenWrt One with case'
sfc.Text: MediaTek MT7981B SoC, with MT7976C wifi, 1 GiB DDR4 RAM, 128 MiB SPI NAND + 4 MiB SPI NOR flash, two Ethernet ports (2.5 GbE and 1 GbE), a USB host port, M.2 2042 for NVMe SSD or similar devices, and mikroBUS expansion header. The OpenWrt offers both PoE (Power over Ethernet) via the 2.5 GbE port, or direct power via the USB-C power port with 12V USB-PD. A convenient USB serial interface is built into the other USB-C port ... providing a switch to separately flash the NOR and NAND portions of the flash memory.

openwrt_forum_183684.beitrag_1_hardware: SOC: MediaTek MT7981B; Wi-Fi: MediaTek MT7976C (2x2 2.4 GHz + 3x3/2x2 + zero-wait DFS 5Ghz); DRAM: 1 GiB DDR4; Flash: 128 MiB SPI NAND+ 4 MiB SPI NOR; Ethernet: 2x RJ45 (2.5 GbE + 1 GbE); USB (host): USB 2.0 (Type-A port); USB (device, console): Holtek HT42B534-2 UART to USB (USB-C port); Storage: M.2 2042 for NVMe SSD (PCIe gen 2 x1); Buttons: 2x (reset + user); Mechanical switch: 1x for boot selection (recovery, regular); LEDs: 2x (PWM driven), 2x ETH Led (GPIO driven); External hardware watchdog: EM Microelectronic EM6324 (GPIO driven); RTC: NXP PCF8563TS (I2C) with battery backup holder(CR1220); Power: USB-PD 12-25V on USB-C port (optional 802.3at/af PoE via RT5400 module); Expansion slots: mikroBUS; Certification: FCC/EC/RoHS compliance; Case: PCB size is compatible to BPi-R4 and the case design can be re-used; JTAG for main SOC: 10-pin 1.27 mm pitch (ARM JTAG/SWD); Antenna connectors: 3x MMCX; Price: aiming for below 100$
openwrt_forum_183684.faq: NAND: main loader + Linux, default boot; NOR write-protected by default (WP jumper), recovery bootloader + Wi-Fi calibration; boot select switch. Kein USB 3.x, weil USB3 und PCIe im SoC geteilt. Console-USB-C: Holtek mit CDC-ACM, keine Treiber noetig. MAC-OUI fuer OpenWrt geplant.
